g12-history-uh7-t1.overview: The Road to Independence and the Rise of Independent States in Africa sits inside Africa Since the 1960s. Independent Africa emerged rapidly after 1960, the focus of Grade 12 History Unit 7 in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it explains the road to independence, from Ghana and Nigeria to the Algerian war. Then it studies politics in independent Africa, including military coups and one-party rule. Next, it covers the economy, society, and the struggle for real economic freedom. Also, it follows the Cold War in Africa, apartheid, and the path from the OAU to the African Union. Students will also learn how independent Africa keeps shaping the continent today.
objectives: Describe the road to independence in West Africa and Algeria.
Explain the causes of military coups in independent Africa.
Discuss the struggle for economic independence after 1960.
Analyse the effects of the Cold War on Africa.
Trace the growth of Pan-Africanism from the OAU to the African Union.
g12-history-uh7-t1.simple:
The Road to Independence and the Rise of Independent States in Africa in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the peaceful road to independence in British and French West Africa.
  • Then the long armed struggle for Algerian independence to 1962.
g12-history-uh7-t1.detailed:
The Road to Independence and the Rise of Independent States in Africa — the essentials. First, the peaceful road to independence in British and French West Africa. Then the long armed struggle for Algerian independence to 1962.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Describe the road to independence in West Africa and Algeria.
  • Explain the causes of military coups in independent Africa.
  • Discuss the struggle for economic independence after 1960.
  • Analyse the effects of the Cold War on Africa.
  • Trace the growth of Pan-Africanism from the OAU to the African Union.
